title: The great circle: the Kav's first will, like a man's taste and his dream house
overview:
The *Kav* goes down in circles (*igulim*) and in a straight line (*yosher*) shaped like a person, and its first circle, *tehiru tata'a*, surrounds all four worlds equally. To explain it the chapter sets out two kinds of will. The simple will in the Essence is like a person's taste or style: it shapes how he will do every kindness and think every thought, yet it is hidden, part of his self-knowledge, with no general and particular. Only when he comes to build does it become a composite will: one general picture of the house, then the kitchen, the sink, down to the *mezuza* on the door.

Above, *tehiru ila'a* is G-d's knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in any way. After the *tzimtzum* comes the choice: this world, all the way to *Moshiach*, as one *ratzon kadum* that includes every detail, even each hair and each leaf in the wind. Everything after it, *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, down to the weather today, is only a means to that goal. That a will can be cut off from its goal is the root of *Tohu*.

terms.gloss: circles: the ten concentric circles the Kav makes as it goes down, like the soul before it comes into the body
the straight line: the sefiros in the form of a person, three lines, like the soul in the body with each power in its own kli
the lower purity: the first circle after the hiyuli Kav, the ultimate goal; self-knowledge of how something separate relates to Him
the raw potential from which all the particular drawings-down branch off
the simple will in the Essence, still one with it; it cannot yet be called a general thought
the absolute will: like a person's taste or style, which shapes every choice and stays hidden
the composite will: a will for something in the world, with a general thing, details and priorities
self-knowledge: knowing what you will want because you know yourself
the upper purity: before the tzimtzum, only G-d's knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in any way
the original will: the ultimate goal, of which everything after it is only a detail and a means
the encompassing light; the first circle surrounds all four worlds equally

sections.title: Circles and the straight line: the first circle is tehiru tata'a
sections.summary: The chapter now explains the *makifim* and *pnimiyim* in the *Kav*: the ten circles (*igulim*) it makes as it goes down, and the straight line (*yosher*) in the form of a person. The first circle, right after the *hiyuli Kav*, is *tehiru tata'a*, the general *makif* over all four worlds equally: the ultimate goal of the whole chain.

phrases.he: (טז) והנה מעתה יש להבין בפרטי ענין הקו וחוט זה, איך שיש בו בחינת מקיפים ופנימיים
phrases.en: Now we're going to explain the *inyan* of *igulim v'yosher*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים מתעגל וחוזר ומתעגל כו' (כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות)

blocks.text: A nice *perek*: short, simple, one *inyan* most people find *geshmak* (tasty). **Now we're going to explain the inyan of igulim v'yosher**: the circles and the straight line, the *makifim* and *pnimiyim* of the *Kav*.

As *Etz Chaim* says, it "circles and returns and circles": the *hiyuli Kav* goes down a little and circles, ten times, the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* of *Adam Kadmon*; then *yosher*. Every world has ten *sefiros* of each, two separate chains.

blocks.question: Is it like a spring?
blocks.text: No: concentric circles with a line through them. It does not spiral; each circle is full and closes, and the *Kav*, coming down one side, goes on to make the next.

blocks.title: Water filling carved troughs
blocks.text:
From the side of the *reshimu* the circles are set up from below upward and are not connected at all; when *yosher* comes down, the *Kav* starts from the top, and in the light they are connected.

As if troughs were carved in the shape of circles and water came down from the top: it fills the first trough, overflows to the next and goes around it. What makes the light stop and circle in each place? The *reshimu* has already carved an *igul* there. It does not fill the inside, only runs around the rim, like a marble run. That line is the *yosher* of the *igulim*.

These are the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* as they are in the light. Over them runs a parallel chain, *yosher*: *sefiros* in the shape of a person, the three lines of *Chabad*, *Chagas*, *Nehi*, *chachma* on the right and *bina* on the left.

The two overlap: the *igulim* start a little higher, from about their *bina* connect to *yosher*, and the rest share its place.

blocks.title: The soul before and in the body
blocks.text:
The *igulim* are like the soul before it enters the body; *yosher*, the soul in the body, each part with its own *kli* (vessel), making a *partzuf*. In the soul all ten powers are one and happen together: willing and walking are the same, since wanting is already being drawn. In the body each is distinct, tied to its *kli*, and can be appreciated.

This chapter and the next three will make it clear.

phrases.he: ובחינת מקיף ועיגול הראשון
phrases.en: in the first circle, right after the *hiyuli Kav*, there's the first circle.

phrases.he: הוא הנקרא טהירו תתאה כו',
phrases.en: That's called the lower purity.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת המקיף הכללי שמקיף לד' עולמות דאבי''ע בשווה
phrases.en: This is the general *makif* that surrounds the four worlds of *ABYA* equally.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: like it says in *Etz Chaim*.

blocks.text: **In the first circle, right after the hiyuli Kav**, **that's called the lower purity**, *tehiru tata'a*: the first *gilui* (revelation) of will for the *hishtalshelus* after the *tzimtzum*, the general *makif*, *sovev kol almin*, the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*. The *reshis hakav*, the *kav hamida* (line of measure) before it, is only a *hiyuli*.

blocks.title: The teacher's ultimate goal
blocks.text: With his system for dividing the subject into levels to measure the student, the teacher makes his first circle: the ultimate goal of this *hishtalshelus*.

blocks.title: Rabbi Chodakov and the shliach to South Africa
blocks.text: This is the unrealistic goal of the Rabbi Chodakov story from the *farbrengen*: a *shliach* (emissary) going to South Africa said he would see what to do when he got there. First set your pure, unrealistic goal, what you want essentially; then make it fit.
So the teacher first works out what the students should ultimately come out with: the all-encompassing desire including any scenario in this classroom, this *hishtalshelus*.

**This is the general makif that surrounds the four worlds of ABYA equally**, usually called *sovev kol almin*; the light before the *tzimtzum*, sometimes called that too, is no *sovev* over a *pnimi*, as will be explained.

sections.title: The Kav as one general thought that sees to the end
sections.summary: First the *Kav* as a whole: one *hiyuli* from which all the particular drawings-down branch off. It is like a general thought that sees to the end of all generations at a glance, as a man who wants a house already wants the kitchen, the sink and the running water.

phrases.he: ותחלה יש להקדים
phrases.en: but first we have to explain,

phrases.he: כללות ענין הקו הזה, איך שהוא בחינת היולי כללי לכל הסתעפות המשכות פרטיים הרבה שמסתעפים ממנו עד סוף העשיה כו' כנזכר לעיל
ויובן זה על דרך משל הידוע בענין מחשבה כללית
שבמחשבה זו הכללית צופה ומביט עד סוף כל הדורות בסקירה א'
phrases.en: that with this general thought Hashem sees the whole *hishtalshelus*, with the whole history of mankind, all the way to the end,

phrases.he: (ובלשון הרמב''ם היינו מה שבידיעת עצמו יודע את כל הנבראים
phrases.en: This is what the *Rambam* describes, that by knowing Himself He knows all the *nivra'im*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.text: **But first we have to explain** the *Kav* as one general *hiyuli* for everything that branches off (*mistaef*) from it, to the end of *Asiya*.

It is understood from the known *mashal* of a general thought: **with this general thought Hashem sees the whole hishtalshelus**, the whole history of mankind to the end of the seventh millennium, past *Moshiach* (the end of the sixth). It is called *ratzon kadum* or *machshava kduma*. In the Rambam's words, **by knowing Himself He knows all the nivra'im** (the created beings).

blocks.title: Do you want a sink in your kitchen?
blocks.text: How can one thought include everything? Ask a man who wants a house whether he wants a kitchen: of course, what kind of house has no kitchen? A sink in the kitchen? What kind of kitchen has no sink? Running water in the sink? So through the whole house. The word "house" is one thought that includes every detail, even less obvious ones, because he wants *his* house: knowing himself, what he likes, he knows what he wants in it.

blocks.title: 126,282 hairs on his head
blocks.text: So if G-d wants a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below), does He want this person in it? How could it be without him? With 126,282 hairs on his head? "He wouldn't be Moishe without that." All the details are included so.

sections.title: Two kinds of will: the simple will is a person's taste, the composite will has priorities
sections.summary: The simple will in the Essence is like a person's taste or style: it already shapes how he will do every kindness and think every thought, but it is hidden and has no general and particular. Only when it comes to action does it become a composite will (*ratzon murkav*): a general thought with particulars under it, circle within circle.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים ידוע
שיש ב' מיני רצון
phrases.en: There's two types of desires.

phrases.he: א' רצון הפשוט שבעצמות
phrases.en: One is the simple *ratzon* that's in the *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: שנכלל בעצמותו ממש,
שלא נקרא עדיין בשם בחינת מחשבה ורצון כללי
phrases.en: You can't call it a general thought or general *ratzon* yet,

phrases.he: כי מתאחד עדיין בעצמותו ממש
phrases.en: still one with his *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: כמו גם שהוחלט רצון זה כבר בעצמו
phrases.en: even the way that he has already predetermined in himself, so to speak,

phrases.he: איך לעשות דבר חסד פלוני
או איך לדבר ולחשוב אותו
phrases.en: or what he's going to say, and what he's going to think.

phrases.he: או להשכיל שכל פרטי
phrases.en: or also the way that each person understands things in different ways.

phrases.he: או להיות לו רצון ותענוג בדבר כו'
phrases.en: or whether he's going to enjoy something or not enjoy something,

blocks.text: **There's two types of desires.** **One is the simple ratzon that's in the Atzmus**, the *ratzon hapashut*: not yet a general thought or will, **still one with his Atzmus**.

It includes **even the way that he has already predetermined in himself, so to speak**, to do a kindness: his taste, the *ratzon hamuchlat* (absolute will). Not a desire about the world but self-knowledge, who he is and how he wants to express himself, an estimation like *Kadmon*.
So he knows that, if it comes up, he will want to give the man the coat; know someone well and you can predict him. That is *Kadmon*, the *ratzon hamuchlat*.

From *Kadmon* a little comes out, not *b'pnimiyus* (inwardly): taste is no desire for a thing yet but bears on all he does, **or what he's going to say, and what he's going to think**. His thinking carries his biases: different people think about a situation each his own way.

**Or also the way that each person understands things in different ways**: Rashi, Tosafos, each has his own *shita* (approach). **Or whether he's going to enjoy something or not**, what he will like and hate: all is included in his taste.

phrases.he: הגם שמתחבר רצון המוחלט הזה אל התפשטות הרצון בדבר הפרטי
phrases.en: even though this taste connects to the actual desire, it influences it,

phrases.he: אבל נשאר כלול בהעלם עצמותו
phrases.en: but it stays really hidden.

phrases.he: ועל כן אין בו עדיין בחינת כלל ופרט כו'
phrases.en: and that therefore their taste does not have a *klal u'prat*.

blocks.text: **Even though this taste connects to the actual desire, it influences it, but it stays really hidden.**

blocks.title: The artist's style
blocks.text: An artist's style is nothing tangible: his painting is shaped by it, but the painting is not his style, and you cannot copy it or say what it is. People who try to work out their style and do it find "it comes out fake."

Style is being yourself, naturally; books on writing and art say the style is the person himself. *Davka* (precisely) when you let yourself come out freely, putting nothing on, not even the way you see yourself, it shows in everything. Yet you cannot point to it: a painting is impressionistic, not impressionism.

So taste shapes every desire, but no desire expresses the whole taste.

**And that therefore their taste does not have a klal u'prat** (general and particular). In a house, the main thing is the building and roof, protection from the elements; then furniture and utilities; then paint, carpet or wood floor; then the bathroom drapes.

All of it is shaped by taste. But an actual will has a main thing: the first circle is for a house, a general picture of one. Inside are circles for the kitchen, living room, dining room, bedroom and bathroom, each with circles of its own, sink and stove, smaller and smaller, down to the bathroom drapes.
Taste shapes every stage equally: every choice of how, big or small, comes from his *ratzon hamuchlat* and expresses it like anything else.

phrases.he: רק כאשר לאחר זה עולה רצון זה שהוחלט אצלו לבוא לידי מעשה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: but when this *ratzon* is going to come now *b'poel mamash*,

phrases.he: הרי יוצא מהעלמו לגלוי
phrases.en: when it comes *b'poel mamash*, actually do it, then it becomes revealed, *l'gilui*,

phrases.he: אז יבוא הרצון בבחינת כלל ופרט,
phrases.en: then there's a general thing and there's the particulars,

phrases.he: דהיינו מחשבה כללית
phrases.en: first there's the general thought

phrases.he: שכוללת כל ענין המעשה מראש לסוף בסקירה א'
phrases.en: that includes everything at once,

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתחלק בו רצונות פרטיים
phrases.en: then it divides to particular desires,

phrases.he: ולכל רצון שכל ומדות כו'
phrases.en: and each one has its own *sechel* and *middos* and everything,

phrases.he: ובאין זה אחר זה בהשתלשלות
phrases.en: and they come one after the other,

phrases.he: זה עליון מקיף לתחתון,
phrases.en: the upper one encompassing the lower one,

phrases.he: כאשר יהיה האופן בתוך האופן כו'
phrases.en: like a circle inside of a circle, concentric circles.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא רצון המורכב שיש בו כלל ופרט
phrases.en: that's called a *ratzon murkav*, a complex *ratzon*.

blocks.text: Before it comes **b'poel mamash** (into actual deed) there is no general and particular: knowing someone well, you could work out his dream house before he ever thought of one.

And what you recognize is how his taste would come out in the society we live in now. The same person in another time would express the same taste differently: instead of a nice, big mansion, he would want a hut if he were a tribal chief in Africa.

sensitivity.reason: Illustrates another time and place with "a hut if he were a tribal chief in Africa"; not meant as disparaging, but a stereotype of Africa a public edition may prefer to drop. As in chapter 18, the publishable text keeps the hut and drops only "in Africa".
sensitivity.publishable: And what you recognize is how his taste would come out in the society we live in now. The same person in another time would express the same taste differently: instead of a nice, big mansion, he would want a hut if he were a tribal chief.

blocks.text: **When it comes b'poel mamash, actually do it, then it becomes revealed**, with general and particular, priorities: **first there's the general thought that includes everything at once**, **then it divides to particular desires**, each with its *sechel* and *middos* (intellect and emotions), one after the other, **the upper one encompassing the lower one** as a detail serving it, **like a circle inside of a circle, concentric circles.**

A general will for the house, a particular one for the kitchen, and within it for the sink: **that's called a ratzon murkav, a complex ratzon**, made of many parts. Taste is a simple will, *ratzon pashut*; actually wanting something in the world is complex, details within details, so there is already a *klal* and a *prat*.

*Murkav* also means priorities. Something simple from the essence is a *nekuda* (a point); here desires conflict, this for the sake of that, "a whole bubble." Each choice comes from his *ratzon hamuchlat*.

But the way it comes out physically is *murkav*. As will be said, perhaps at the start of the next chapter, the *ratzon hamuchlat* is really for himself, self-expression: he is comfortable *davka* a certain way, wants a certain atmosphere, and his house expresses him.

sections.title: The mashal: a man who wants to build a great building
sections.summary: The taste a man already has for a building is still within himself, as if it did not exist; the house is not yet wanted. When he comes to build, the details he had already settled appear, first as one general picture, then will after will down to the last screw and the *mezuza* on the door.

phrases.he: ויובן זה על דרך משל הידוע,
אדם שרוצה לבנות בנין גדול
phrases.en: a person wants to build a big building,

phrases.he: כפי הרצון שהוחלת מכבר אצלו
phrases.en: according to his taste,

phrases.he: להיות בו אופנים מיוחדים דוקא
phrases.en: he wants it to be specially designed for the way he wants it.

phrases.he: שאותו הרצון שהוחלט אצלו מכבר,
phrases.en: that this taste that he had already decided before,

phrases.he: הגם שהוא בא במדה ותענוג מיוחד
phrases.en: even though in a way it is like defined, that each person has a certain thing, they enjoy things in a certain way,

phrases.he: באופן כך וכך,
וממילא בשכל ומדות בא בשיעור ומדה כו',
phrases.en: and since he enjoys things a certain way, that automatically influences that his *sechel* leans to try to find that; everything is in line with that.

phrases.he: אך כל זה הוא השיעור וההחלט שבעצמותו עדיין,
phrases.en: that's all still within his essence,

phrases.he: ונכלל בעצמו
phrases.en: and it's really part of himself,

phrases.he: והיה כלא היה כו'
phrases.en: it's like it doesn't exist; he doesn't actually have a desire yet for a house.

blocks.text: **A person wants to build a big building, according to his taste**, **specially designed for the way he wants it**: a dream house, or a dream Chabad house.

**This taste that he had already decided before**, defined in that he enjoys things a certain way so that **his sechel leans to try to find that**, is **still within his essence**, **really part of himself**: **it's like it doesn't exist; he doesn't actually have a desire yet for a house.**

Knowing him, you know how he would want it, but he has no desire yet, no thought of anything outside himself: it is *yedias atzmo* (self-knowledge). You know what you want in a house by thinking of what makes you happy, how you want to feel; that is its *pnimiyus* (inner side).
It comes from a *teva* (nature), so to speak, that he set in his personality *b'kadmonius*: the form he chose to express himself in, which comes out in the world according to each situation.

That is *teshuva*: reconnecting the outer desires to their source, like hitting the reset button. The higher the desire you change, the more flexible everything under it; at the essence everything is, because the inner desire there is to show you have *bechira* (free choice), your *etzem* stuck in nothing.

The usual order of *avoda*: first a person uses his nature, the way he is, for good. Next he breaks out of it, not by *iskafya* (forcing himself against it) but by freeing himself: the personality he takes for himself is a role he acts out, a costume, and he can choose another.

So Avraham had to do *gevura*, and Yaakov, an *ish tam* (a simple, wholesome man), had "to lie and cheat" Esav and Lavan: they had to act against their nature. What it was for Yitzchak, he is not sure. *Davka* when a person does this, he reveals his *etzem*.

sensitivity.reason: Says Yaakov Avinu had "to lie and cheat" Esav and Lavan; the point is a Torah one, but the blunt wording about a patriarch may need his approval in print.
sensitivity.publishable: So Avraham had to do *gevura*, and Yaakov, an *ish tam* (a simple, wholesome man), had to deal deceptively with Esav and Lavan: they had to act against their nature. What it was for Yitzchak, he is not sure. *Davka* when a person does this, he reveals his *etzem*.

blocks.title: The Purim costume
blocks.text: In a Purim costume you feel free, since it does not reflect on you. So from the *yechida* a person sees all his *partzufim*, his roles, as costumes he can take off.

So the Rebbe was very unpredictable, acting differently with each person and situation, at every extreme: most private and most public, most liberal and most conservative. Normally these are contradictions, but when you reveal the essence, "you can have 100% of both," not 50-50 or all of one.

phrases.he: רק כאשר לאחר זמן באה מחשבה זו לבא למעשה,
phrases.en: but when later he actually thinks, "Oh, I want to build a house,"

phrases.he: ניכר בו התחלקות אותן אופנים שונים ממש שכבר הוחלט אצלו בכל פרטיהם
phrases.en: Now then you see everything that was already decided there with all the details.

phrases.he: רק שמתחלה בא הרצון הזה בדרך כלל
phrases.en: first comes as a general thought,

phrases.he: שיהיה לו בנין בציור כך וכך
phrases.en: he wants this general type of a house,

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתחלק בו רצון פרטי
phrases.en: and then he plans out where he wants the house to be, how he's gonna pay for it, exactly how he's gonna decorate it, all the details he thinks of later.

phrases.he: לכל ענין פרטי
phrases.en: for each detail, like the kitchen, and the sink, and whatever.

phrases.he: ויורד ובא בסדר והדרגה מכלל הראשון
phrases.en: from the first general *klal*, like the *ratzon* for a house,

phrases.he: שכולל הכל בסקירה א'
לפרט רצון שהוא נקרא כלל לגבי רצונות המסתעפים ממנו
phrases.en: Then he goes from the general *ratzon* of a house to a detail of that, like the kitchen, but that's then a general thing for everything that branches off from it,

phrases.he: עד שבא אל רצון ושכל פרטי היותר אחרון
phrases.en: until it comes to the last screw,

phrases.he: שבסוף מעשה בכלות הכל כו' ודי למבין.
phrases.en: putting up the *mezuza* on his front door when he's finished everything.

blocks.text: **But when later he actually thinks, "Oh, I want to build a house,"** **now then you see everything that was already decided there with all the details.**

blocks.title: Advertising
blocks.text:
The same idea on a lower level is advertising. It does not look for someone who wants a car now; it wants him to form, subconsciously, a positive association with the name, so that one day he thinks of it first, or picks it between two. It gives the product an image, being free, being put together, so that people who want to express themselves through that image choose it.

The real *ratzon hamuchlat* is the image a person wants to express himself as; advertisers do not set it, "they're just trying to tap into that."

His *ratzon hamuchlat* now comes out *l'poel* (into action), in a house in this world. It **first comes as a general thought**, this type of house; **and then he plans out where he wants the house to be, how he's gonna pay for it, exactly how he's gonna decorate it**, each detail, kitchen and sink.

It goes down by levels **from the first general klal, like the ratzon for a house**, to a detail like the kitchen, itself general for what branches from it, **until it comes to the last screw**: the *mezuza* on the front door when everything is finished.

That is the ten *sefiros* of *igulim*: the first circle, the will for the whole *dira b'tachtonim*, splits into wills for *Atzilus* and *Beriya*, each into its ten *sefiros*, down to each person and little creature G-d made.

sections.title: The nimshal above: tehiru ila'a is the taste still within the Essence
sections.summary: Before the *tzimtzum*, in *tehiru ila'a*, G-d has the knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in any way, like the taste in the simple will: not yet a will for anything outside Himself, so it cannot even be called a general thought. *Tehiru tata'a*, after the *tzimtzum*, is the choice of this world: still self-knowledge, but of how something separate relates to Him, so a lower purity.

phrases.he: והנמשל מכל זה יובן למעלה בהפרש שבין בחינת טהירו עילאה ובין בחינת טהירו תתאה שלאחר הצמצום

blocks.text: The *nimshal*: the difference between *tehiru ila'a*, the essential simple will with *Yachid* and *Kadmon* (*Kadmon* the part relating to what follows), and *tehiru tata'a* after the *tzimtzum*, the actual revealed will.

Before the *tzimtzum* is the *etzem*, holding like a *hiyuli* G-d's knowledge and ability to reveal Himself any way, our world included, should He choose. The *tzimtzum* and *reshimu* picked the way. The first *ratzon kadum*, the result of *tzimtzum*, *reshimu* and *Kav*, is that choice, starting as the general thought of our world.

That is the product: our world in its totality, G-d as Creator of man, *galus* (exile), *geula* (redemption), *dira b'tachtonim*, all the way to *Moshiach*: one way He could reveal Himself, *tehiru tata'a*. Revealing the *etzem* is higher, not in it, "I don't think."

phrases.he: דמה ששיער בעצמו בכח בטהירו עילאה כו'
phrases.en: that in *tehiru ila'a* it's just that Hashem has in His ability the knowledge of how to do it and the ability to do it.

phrases.he: הוא כמו ההחלט ברצון הפשוט שבעצמות הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like a taste,

phrases.he: שעדיין לא בא כלל לבחינת התפשטות חוץ מן העצמות עדיין
phrases.en: It's not at all an actual *ratzon* for something separate from Himself.

phrases.he: וגם שיתחבר מרצון המוחלט הזה אל התפשטות הרצון שאחר כך,
phrases.en: even though this connects to the *hispashtus* of the *ratzon*

phrases.he: מכל מקום נשאר כלול בהעלם עצמות דאור אין סוף
phrases.en: The *ratzon muchlat* stays really hidden.

phrases.he: ועל כן למעלה הוא מבחינת כלל להיות נקרא צופה ומביט בסקירה א' כו'.
phrases.en: Therefore, at that stage you can't even call it a general thing, a general thought of our world that's in a *skira achas*.

blocks.text: *Tehiru ila'a* means **Hashem has in His ability the knowledge of how to do it and the ability to do it**, **like a taste**: **it's not at all an actual ratzon for something separate from Himself.** Though it connects to the will's spreading out, **the ratzon muchlat stays really hidden**, being no *makif* and *pnimi*; even *Kadmon*'s estimation is not revealed.

**Therefore, at that stage you can't even call it a general thing, a general thought of our world that's in a skira achas** (one glance): it is only *yedias atzmo*, and so *tehiru ila'a* is completely pure. *Tehiru tata'a* is G-d seeing the world as His expression: still *yedias atzmo*, but with a *nivra* (a created being) in it, a lower purity.
You are still thinking of yourself: the *ratzon kadum* is "a ratzon for a home," the feeling, not yet a house. Picturing an actual house by your society comes in *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.title: The clingy baby
blocks.text: At a certain age a person wants independence, to settle down: "a person without a house is not a person." In the *ratzon hamuchlat* you know it even of a clingy baby who will not let go of his mother: one day he will want his own house and only visit. You know because you know people; the child does not, and would not believe you.

At first it is not a will for an apartment but an uneasiness: he feels unsettled and looks for what will fit, until, visiting someone with his own place, he feels that independence and realizes that was it.

So the *ratzon kadum* is already a will for a particular *taanug* (delight) fulfilled in the world outside, only looking for what will do it. That is why the *igulim* are like the soul: not yet enclothed in the tangible world.

sections.title: The second will: the Kav and its first circle, the ratzon kadum
sections.summary: After the *tzimtzum*, the simple will comes to spread forth: that is the *hiyuli Kav*, a general system of priorities. Its first product is the ultimate goal, the first circle, *tehiru tata'a*, which includes every particular will and is called *ratzon kadum*: everything after it is only a means to it.

phrases.he: אך הרצון הב' הוא אחר הצמצום הנזכר לעיל
שעולה רצון הפשוט המוחלט שבעצמות לבא לידי בחינת התפשטות
phrases.en: that something from this *ratzon pashut* came to actually do it, that Hashem decided, picked what He's going to actually do.

phrases.he: הוא בחינת הקו וחוט ההיולי שכולל כל המשכות פרטיות שבו מראשו לסופו כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: The second will, after the *tzimtzum*: **that Hashem decided, picked what He's going to actually do.** That is the *hiyuli Kav*, including all the particular drawings-down from start to end.

That is the *Kav* in general. The *reshimu*, with the head of the *Kav*, is the goal; the *Kav* is the way to reach it, a system of priorities, so that together you know how to react in any situation. Their first result is your ultimate goal, the *ratzon kadum*.

phrases.he: ובחינת מקיף הראשון שבו הוא הנקרא טהירו תתאה,
שזהו כמשל רצון הכללי לבנין גדול כולל כל מה שבפרטיו מראשו לסופו בבת א'
ואחר כך מתחלק בו בסדר והדרגה מכלל לפרט
phrases.en: Then this gets split up,

phrases.he: על דרך משל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like in the *mashal* we said about the house.

blocks.text: Its first *makif*, *tehiru tata'a*, is like the general will for a great building, including all its details; in a life, the desire for fulfillment, the top priority. **Then this gets split up.**

This is the *etzem* of the *yechida*, the *Moshiach* within each person: find it and you are redeemed, fulfilled. It splits into lesser priorities by your *Kav*, down to daily life, **like in the mashal we said about the house.**

phrases.he: והיינו כמו כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט ההיולי לבא לגלוי דוקא, היה כולל כל פרטי הרצונות
phrases.en: And this is the *inyan* that when he had a particular *ratzon*, it came out, he already had all the things that he wants to do included in that.

phrases.he: והוא הרצון הכולל כולם,
phrases.en: and this first *ratzon* that comes out *b'gilui* includes them all,

phrases.he: ונקרא רצון קדום לכל מה שבא אחריו
phrases.en: This is called the original *ratzon* for everything that comes after.

blocks.text: When it rose in His will to come *davka* into revelation, **this first ratzon that comes out b'gilui includes them all**: **this is called the original ratzon for everything that comes after**, original because all the rest are its details, means to this goal.

That is the difference between *kadum* and *rishon*: *rishon* (first) comes first in any order; *kadum* means what follows has no meaning but to fulfill it. The will for money serves a deeper one, to buy what you need, to do as you like without worry, or stature; trace all the wills back and you reach one essential desire, the inner goal.

sections.title: Down to the last detail, all included in the first circle around all four worlds
sections.summary: From the *ratzon kadum* come the particular wills: for *Atzilus* with its ten *sefiros*, still hidden until it is revealed, then to create *Beriya*, down to the last will of *Asiya*. All of them are included in the first circle, the beginning of the *Kav*, which surrounds the four worlds equally because they are all equally only a means to its goal. That they can be cut off from it is the root of *Tohu*.

phrases.he: ואחר כך בא רצון זה דרך פרט,
phrases.en: And then the details are revealed,

phrases.he: כמו הרצון להאציל
phrases.en: like the desire for *Atzilus*,

phrases.he: ובו כלול עשר ספירות בכל פרטיהם
phrases.en: and this includes ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: ועדיין הכל בהעלם
phrases.en: but you didn't actually do *Atzilus* yet.

phrases.he: עד שבא לידי גלוי שהוא כשנאצל האור בבחינת האצילות כו'
phrases.en: then it comes *b'gilui*: that's when he actually was *ne'etzal*.

blocks.text: **And then the details are revealed, like the desire for Atzilus**: like the newly married man with the architect. Asked what you are looking for, you talk not about a house but about yourself, what you like. **And this includes ten sefiros** with all their details.

blocks.title: Out to dinner, and the door
blocks.text: **But you didn't actually do Atzilus yet**: all is hidden. Going out to dinner, where does the *ratzon* to open the restaurant door come from? It was in the *ratzon* to go there: all later wills are in the original desire.

blocks.title: Shall we drive to the real estate agent?
blocks.text: Ask a man who wants a house whether he wants a kitchen, or whether to drive to the real estate agent: of course. He did not think of the details, but whatever it takes, he wants done.

So in *tehiru tata'a* they are there not in actuality but as one general thought holding all the later ones. In actuality they are the later circles, the *igulim* of *Atzilus* and *Beriya*, split into each thing. To relate to a limited physical manifestation you must pick a form, really a *kli*: more like *tehiru tata'a*.

There is a *yechida* with a name, the *ratzon kadum* of *Adam Kadmon*, a picture of your essence, and one without, the real essence, *Yachid*, like before the *tzimtzum*. It includes that you can have *chesed*, like *Echad*, and *Malchus*, like *Kadmon*: so he picks those two wills.

You can pick a general, abstract desire beyond form, including everything, or a particular *kli* to express it, like *Kadmon*, or *Malchus*. In the *etzem* these two, like *chesed* and *gevura*, are only a *yecholes* (an ability), undivided: the *etzem* is just the *etzem*, so it can do both. The *tzimtzum* chooses which *Echad* and *Kadmon*; its result is *tehiru tata'a*.

You do not yet know it is a house, only that you want to express a certain *inyan* of yourself, the *taanug* of independence, say, and you look until you find the desire for a house to match. That is the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, your worldview and self-image. A person usually means one already limited to ten *sefiros*, and those limits start in the *ratzon kadum* of *Adam Kadmon*: "the first time it's like a person."

That came from the *tzimtzum*; the chain in the person runs with the chain in the worlds: G-d's *ratzon kadum* gave the soul its form, and the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon* how it enters the body, its mission.

The *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon* is *Moshiach* as a person; its *igulim*, the *pnimiyus*, are the *dira b'tachtonim*, the *nekuda*; how it is expressed in our world is what the *halacha* and *Midrashim* say of *Moshiach*.
**Then it comes b'gilui: that's when he actually was ne'etzal** (emanated): *Atzilus* reveals the ten *sefiros* of its *igulim* included in the original.

phrases.he: ואחר כך הרצון לברוא
phrases.en: the next *ratzon* is the *ratzon* to create,

phrases.he: יש מאין כו'
ובו שכל ומדות כו'
phrases.en: and then it also has ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: עד הרצון היותר אחרון
phrases.en: so the final most *ratzon*,

phrases.he: שהוא כל אשר חפץ עשה כו', סוף הכל

blocks.text: Then **the next ratzon is the ratzon to create**: what will fulfill your desires. To swim, a pool; for *farbrengens*, a roomy dining room with no carpet, so messes clean up. That is the desire for *Beriya*, its *igulim*: to create *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing), **and then it also has ten sefiros.**

Down to **the final most ratzon**, "all that He desired, He did": in the house, the *mezuza*, the furniture, the last touches; in the world, the little details of daily physical life, like today's weather: *Asiya*.

phrases.he: וכל פרטים הללו נכללו ברצון הקדום
phrases.en: all these details, they were all included in the original desire

phrases.he: שבא בבחינת השפעה על כל פנים אחר הצמצום
phrases.en: which is already an actual *hashpaa*, an actual thing that relates to the outside world, and after the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת ראשית הקו כו',
phrases.en: and this first circle is considered the beginning of the *Kav*, it's the first *gilui* of the *Kav*.

phrases.he: והיינו עיגול הראשון שאחר המשכת ראשית הקו ההיולי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: this is the first circle after the *hiyuli Kav*,

blocks.text: **All these details, they were all included in the original desire**, already an actual *hashpaa* (influence) relating to the outside world, after the *tzimtzum*. **This first circle is considered the beginning of the Kav, it's the first gilui of the Kav** (*reshis hakav* can also mean the *hiyuli Kav*): the top priority.
*HaYom Yom* says every detail of creation, even a blade of grass swaying in the wind, is not only *hashgacha pratis* (individual Divine providence) but necessary for creation's whole intent.

blocks.title: The leaves in this corner
blocks.text: Ask G-d, who wants a *dira b'tachtonim*, whether the leaves in this corner should blow back and forth 300,267,371 times. Of course: "how else could I have a *dira b'tachtonim* if it wasn't just like that?"

Every *prat* is there for a reason we will appreciate only through the seventh millennium: each detail of creation exists as a tool of this will, fulfilling a part of it, or it would not exist. **This is the first circle after the hiyuli Kav.**

phrases.he: שנקרא מקיף כללי לכללות כל הד' עולמות דאבי''ע,
phrases.en: this first *ratzon* is called the general *makif* for all the four worlds of *ABYA*,

phrases.he: שמקיף אותם בשוה
phrases.en: that it surrounds them all equally, meaning that they're all equally just a means to accomplish this goal.

phrases.he: שנקרא מחשבה כללית שצופה ומביט בסקירה א' מראש לסוף הכל כו'
phrases.en: it's called a general thought that it sees everything in one glance.

blocks.text: **This first ratzon is called the general makif for all the four worlds of ABYA**, **that it surrounds them all equally, meaning that they're all equally just a means to accomplish this goal.** The *Kav* sets their order, but each will comes straight from the *ratzon hamuchlat*, so a person's wills "can jump out of place."

blocks.title: The son who forgot his mother
blocks.text: A boy from a very poor family dreams of one day supporting his mother. He makes a lot of money, gets caught up in the desire for it and forgets her; he will not give her money, maybe not even himself, and becomes a miser. Or people deep in business forget their families, when working was only the means for what they really enjoy: Torah and *mitzvos*, family, the people who matter.

How does a person forget? That is *Tohu*: each will has the *etzem* in it, so you can lock into one, absorbed in its *taanug*, forgetting all else. Means to an end is *tikun* (rectification). "But that's also part of the bechira."

*Tohu* is so powerful because it takes maturity to appreciate the deeper *taanug* of priorities. *Igulim* and *yosher* are the root of *Tohu* and *tikun*, spoken of later. As for this first circle, **it's called a general thought that it sees everything in one glance.**

phrases.he: וזהו ביאור ענין כללי לכללות ענין הקו הזה
phrases.en: this is the general idea of the *Kav*,

phrases.he: ופרטי אופניו במה שמתעגל וחוזר ומתעגל כו'
phrases.en: and the details of how it circles and circles again,

phrases.he: יובן לפי אופן משל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: now we can understand the general idea of what we mean by concentric circles by this *mashal*.

phrases.he: וכמו שיתבאר בסמוך בעזרת ה׳ ודי למבין:
phrases.en: and now we'll explain more about it in the next chapter

blocks.text: **This is the general idea of the Kav**: general first, then measuring out details. **And the details of how it circles and circles again** are understood by this *mashal* of concentric circles; the next chapter explains circle inside circle, and how *yosher* is the opposite.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the *igulim* and the *yosher* of the *Kav*, and what do the water in the carved troughs and the soul before and in the body show about them?
Why is the first circle, *tehiru tata'a*, compared to a teacher's ultimate goal, and what does the story of Rabbi Chodakov and the *shliach* teach about it?
How is the *ratzon hamuchlat* like an artist's style, and why does it have no general and particular?
What makes a will *murkav*, and how does the will for a house show it?
Why is *tehiru tata'a* a lower purity than *tehiru ila'a*, though both are G-d's self-knowledge?
Why does the first circle surround the four worlds equally, and how can a person's wills "jump out of place"?

notes.text: A listener is present in these tapes, unlike chapter 10: a student asks "A spring?" (49 w181-182), and he answers questions we do not hear ("I told you this story that he said there?" 49 w1143-1186; "This is the machshava kduma, yeah" 49 w1564-1570; "That's already muchlat, yeah. Murkav, right." 50 w1433-1438; "Yeah, you can open it" 50 w1849-1853). Only the spring question is audible enough for a question block.

The transcript hears "tehiru" as "tziyur" ("tziyur ila'a", "tziyur tata'a", 51 w658-720; "tziyur d'tata'a", 52 w329-717) and line 31's "tehiru tata'a" as "Toras Hashem" (51 w1877-1886). The blocks write tehiru ila'a and tehiru tata'a, as the chapter text has them.

Phrases he reads without translating keep their Hebrew alone: line 2, the end of line 4 and all of line 5, the start of line 7, the end of the first clause of line 8, "b'ofen kach v'kach" in line 18, line 24, the start of line 29 and all of line 30, lines 31 and 32, "yesh me'ayin" in line 38, and the end of line 39. Line 1's only English is his loose "Now we're going to explain the inyan of igulim v'yosher" (49 w67-76), kept for the whole line. Line 9's third phrase cites his rendering some sentences after its reading (49 w2295-2310, where he rereads it), and its last two phrases are in the next tape (50 w4-16, w76-86). Line 37's last phrase cites 52 w1118-1135, long after the line is first read, where he rereads it and says "that's when he actually was ne'etzal". Line 25's second phrase is only "like a taste" (51 w993-995); the sentence breaks off.

Rabbi Chodakov (the transcript's "Rabbi Chadkov") is presumably Rabbi Chaim Mordechai Aizik Chodakov, the Rebbe's chief secretary; the story is told briefly and the shliach is not named. The story is left unflagged: it criticizes no one.

The block on Avraham and Yaakov (50 w2121-2208) is flagged "other" for "Yaakov having to lie and cheat Esav and Lavan": the teaching (they had to act against their nature) is kept, and the publishable text says "deal deceptively". He says he is not sure what it was by Yitzchak. A reviewer may decide this needs no flag. "The most liberal and the most conservative" of the Rebbe's conduct (50 w2277-2332) was judged not to need a flag: it takes no political side.

"Like it says in HaYom Yom, every single detail of creation, even the way a blade of grass swings in the wind ... is necessary for the entire kavana of the beriya" (52 w1492-1542) is reported as he gives it; the reference was not checked.

"Even though this connects to the hispashtus of the ratzon" (line 27): he goes on in Hebrew ("she'yihyeh achar kach"), so the English stops there. "V'ba'in zeh achar zeh b'hishtalshelus" (line 15) is one phrase, because "zeh" repeats; his English covers "one after the other" only.

Reviewer: line 34 is heard by the transcript as "birtzono hapashut d'yihyeh lo bayis lo l'gilui" (51 w2042-2057), a mishearing of "hahiyuli lavo l'gilui"; the block follows the chapter text and no longer speaks of "a house of his own". Line 9's first phrase now ends at "b'atzmo"; "eich la'asos davar chesed ploni" is read without an English of its own (his "how he'll want to do a particular chesed ploni" comes later, 49 w2120-2165, in the explanation). Line 22's "she'kolel hakol b'skira achas" is read without English. The "tribal chief in Africa" remark (50 w886-905) is now flagged other-groups; a human may judge it harmless.
